_comment: The Stop hook checks what the last turn said. See
The command probes for an interpreter rather than naming one. Bare
`python` on a default Windows box is the Microsoft Store stub, which
prints a notice and EXITS 0 -- so the hook silently never ran and its
empty log looked exactly like a clean session. An exit-code chain
cannot catch that, so each candidate is tested by whether it prints.
The project venv comes first because on such a machine it is the only

PreToolUse/AskUserQuestion covers what Stop structurally cannot. A Stop hook fires only on a turn that ends in prose; in a build most turns end in a question, and all 34 findings measured across twelve builds sat on those screens. Same script, same catalog, same log.

hooks.command: for p in "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.venv/Scripts/python.exe" "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.venv/bin/python" "$HOME/.local/bin/python.exe" "$HOME/.local/bin/python" py python3 python; do if [ "$("$p" -c 'print(1)' 2>/dev/null)" = "1" ]; then "$p" "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/language_check.py"; exit $?; fi; done; exit 0
